title: The joy of fish
hook: on a bridge, Zhuangzi and his friend Huizi argue whether anyone can know that fish are happy (Zhuangzi 17)
carry: I know it from the bridge

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Zhuangzi, whose useless tree lived because no carpenter wanted it. Your line was useless, and alive.

Some friends argue with everything. Call the sunset beautiful, and they say, technically, that's just light scattering. Say the dog looks happy, and they ask how anyone could possibly know. It's annoying. And a conversation can be poorer without them. Zhuangzi had a friend like that: Huizi, a sharp logician and his sparring partner. One day the two of them are strolling across a bridge over the Hao River. Zhuangzi leans on the rail, watches the little fish darting below, and says something simple.
screen: `A FRIEND WHO ARGUES WITH EVERYTHING.` → `ZHUANGZI AND HUIZI.` → `A BRIDGE OVER THE HAO.`

segments.voice: Look at the minnows, Zhuangzi says, swimming out and about, so free and easy. That's the joy of fish. Huizi pounces. You're not a fish. How do you know what fish enjoy? Zhuangzi fires back: you're not me. How do you know I don't know what fish enjoy? Huizi is ready. Fine. I'm not you, so I can't know what you know. And you're not a fish. So that settles it: you can't know the joy of fish. And Zhuangzi says: let's go back to where we started. You asked me how I know the joy of fish. So you already knew that I knew it, when you asked. I know it here, from the bridge. Readers have argued about that last move ever since. A cheap trick with words? Partly, and Zhuangzi probably enjoyed that. But there's something real under it. Huizi's kind of knowing stands apart: prove it from the outside, or it doesn't count. Zhuangzi's kind stands somewhere: on this bridge, this afternoon, watching these fish. It's how you know a friend is sad before they say a word. Not proof. Presence. And notice they're both still on the bridge, still friends, still arguing. Later in the book, after Huizi dies, Zhuangzi says that with his friend gone, he has no one left to talk with. The argument was a kind of love. You don't have to choose between their ways of knowing. But it's worth noticing which one you've been using.
screen: `YOU'RE NOT A FISH.` · `YOU'RE NOT ME.` · `KNOWING FROM OUTSIDE, OR FROM HERE.` · `THE ARGUMENT WAS A KIND OF LOVE.` · then, large: `I KNOW IT FROM THE BRIDGE.`

segments.voice: Watch an animal for two minutes: a pet, a bird at the window, a squirrel, even an ant, or if none is near, picture one you know well. Don't name what it's doing or analyze it; just watch the way it moves, the way it pauses. Stand on the bridge, and see what you know from there.
Huizi. Zhuangzi's sharp friend, who argued with him on a bridge about whether anyone can know the joy of fish.
Your line: I know it from the bridge. Some knowing comes from being there, not from proof. Day fifty-three, done.

howItsDone: The debate on the Hao River bridge closes chapter seventeen of the Zhuangzi and is still discussed in Chinese philosophy, read both as a joke about logic and as a teaching about knowing from where you stand.
